text:
Repeated prefixes and replacement draws are dependent observations within users; treating them as independent inflates precision. Cluster-bootstrap literature supports resampling whole users while retaining their observations; hierarchical-bootstrap research addresses additional nested randomness. Applied here, a reproducible protocol would compute paired perturbed-minus-original differences using identical prefixes and candidate sets, average draws within prefixes and prefixes within users, then bootstrap users within each category. Recompute the four-category macro-average for each of 10,000 resamples; publish the seed, weighting rule and percentile interval. This is a proposed adaptation of [cluster bootstrapping](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5965657/) and [hierarchical bootstrapping](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7906290/), not a directly established sequential-recommender standard.

Separate uncertainty across sampled users from Monte Carlo variability across replacements. Keep overlapping prefixes together in the primary user bootstrap; independently resampling prefixes would ignore their temporal dependence. Assess replacement variability through repeated draw banks or justified nested resampling. With only five users per category, report individual user effects, leave-one-user-out sensitivity, and sensitivity to prefix count, perturbation strength and replacement distribution. Additional draws improve estimation for those users but cannot establish population representativeness; small-cluster bootstrap intervals can have [poor coverage](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC535558/).

Perturbations of training histories measure fitted-model sensitivity, not held-out recommendation generalization. Bootstrap intervals cannot remove training-data optimism, temporal leakage or adaptive validation selection. Keep these diagnostics separate from the pinned validation HR@10 and reserve hidden test evaluation for final assessment. Sequential-recommender research documents how [training/evaluation overlap and temporal leakage](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/eval_flaws_recsys23.pdf) can distort apparent performance. All proposed resampling concerns diagnostic measurements from the existing model; no model refitting or prediction averaging is required.
